name: ten Numerative

dimensions.form: Monomorphemic lexeme; base for teen and decade derivation
dimensions.function: Determiner, factor; morphological base for -teen and -ty

projection.target: Ten chapters uses ten directly with a plural nominal. In two tens, the separate cardinal two quantifies two realizations of the value and tens inflects. An independent use of ten does not force either analysis across contexts.
projection.evidence: Reynolds lists ten among the basic determinative forms and uses token nouns to establish separate noun distribution.

curious.title: The word ten
curious.summary: Ten is a single word that other number words, such as -teen and -ty ones, are built from.
curious.body: Ten is a single word that specifies the amount ten. It can stand in front of a plural noun, as in ten chapters, and it's the base that the -teen and -ty numbers are formed from. Ten can also be counted. In two tens, the number two counts two portions of the value ten, and tens takes a plural ending. This dictionary says that ten used on its own doesn't force either analysis in every context.
curious.try: Compare ten chapters with two tens. Which one has an s on ten, and what is two doing in it?

teacher.summary: Explains ten as a basic numerative and how it differs from the noun use in two tens.
teacher.explain: Ten is a monomorphemic lexeme specifying a cardinality of ten. It occurs in all basic numerative positions, including determiner and factor, and is the morphological base for -teen and -ty. Ten chapters uses ten directly with a plural nominal. In two tens, the separate cardinal two quantifies two realizations of the value and tens inflects, as a noun would. This dictionary doesn't force either analysis for an independent use of ten across contexts. It is provisional.
teacher.terms: Cardinal number is the traditional name. This dictionary also uses cardinal noun for the countable use in two tens.

contrasts.note: Ten used directly with a plural noun.
Tens inflects for number and is counted by two.

watch_for: A learner might read tens in two tens as a plural of the determiner in ten chapters, when it takes plural marking as a noun.
A learner might assume a bare ten has one fixed analysis, when this dictionary leaves that open across contexts.
teacher.activity: Students write one phrase with ten before a noun and one with two tens, and explain in their own words what two counts in the second.

cite: Reynolds, Brett, ed. 2026. "ten Numerative." English Constructionary. https://brettreynolds.ca/constructionary/linguist/numerative-ten-001/ (snapshot 2026-11-19, ef810bb).
